AlreadyPresent.description:
Advisory: the patch's content appears to already exist on the
target. Never affects the verdict; q-port and the operator own
the exclusion decision.

content.description: Tier-2 tally: the post-image is (partly) present in the tree.

identical.description: Tier-1 hit: an identical patch landed on the target.

AlreadyPresentSkipped.description:
Why already-present detection could not run. Emitted instead of
silence: an invisible skip would read as "not present".

oneOf.description:
The candidate commit object is absent from the target object
store (an unfetched branch, usually).
The candidate and the target tip share no history.
The target-side walk failed (shallow clone, corrupt object).

ApplyConflictKind.description:
The apply outcomes a divergence predictor consumes, ordered by
severity: a higher variant outranks a lower one on the same path, so
dedup to one conflict per path is a `max`.

ApplyForecast.description:
Per-path apply prediction for one `(commit, series)` row, computed
from the target tree. Present exactly when a target context was
supplied.

paths.description:
Every assessed touched path, including ones absent on the
target (`Conflict { FileAbsent }`).

oneOf.description: Variable identifier (starts with `_` or capital letter).
Atom literal: `foo`, `'quoted atom'`.
Integer literal.
Float literal.
Binary literal: `<<...>>`.
List literal: `[...]`.
Tuple literal: `{...}` (size is the number of elements).
Record reference: `#name{...}`.
String literal: `"..."`.
Anonymous fun: `fun ... end` or `fun mod:f/A`.
Anything the extractor cannot classify. Always matches.

`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`, or `||||||| ` marker present in a
touched file. The cherry-pick driver left a conflict unresolved.

`-export([f/N])` line without a matching clause defining `f/N`.
Compiles, then crashes at runtime on the first call.

BatchQuery.description:
One series queried by the batch. Holds the pin set used during
evaluation so consumers can correlate per-row results.

BatchResult.description: One row in the batch result set.

apply.description:
Apply-axis prediction for this row. `None` means no target
context was supplied, so the axis was not evaluated: never
"clean". A producer with a target context always emits `Some`,
even when the patch touched zero files.

parent_count.description:
Number of parents of the evaluated commit: 1 for plain
commits, 2 for PR merges, 3+ for octopus merges. `None` only
when the envelope was produced by a pre-v7 binary; v7
producers always emit it.

pr_commits.description:
Inner PR-branch commits for 2-parent merge SHAs. `None` for
non-2-parent merges and non-merge SHAs.

Do NOT add `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`. The
`None` vs `Some(vec![])` distinction is wire-load-bearing.

touched_paths.description:
Paths the analysed patch touched, in diff-encounter order.
Always emitted; an empty vec means the patch touched zero
files.

verdict_fingerprint.description:
Stable join key tying this row's verdict to a later build
outcome. Absent for uncacheable rows (`--no-cache`, an
unresolvable pin) and pre-fingerprint producers.

BumpStatus.description: What the snapshot store knows about a bumped-to pin version.

oneOf.description: The bumped dep is not a tracked project; nothing to vet.
No snapshot for the bumped-to version; `note` carries the remedy.
`<<<<<<<` line: start of the local side.
`=======` line: divider between sides.
`>>>>>>>` line: end of the incoming side.
`||||||| ` line: base ancestor marker from a 3-way diff.

ContentPresence.description:
Tier-2 advisory: how much of the patch's post-image already exists
in the named pin's tree. A tally, never a boolean: partial presence
is common and the fraction is the signal.

pin.description:
The pin whose evaluation produced the tally. In cross-branch
mode the self pin resolves to the target branch, so its tally
is the target-tree answer.

DepPinDivergence.description:
A dependency whose `rabbitmq-components.mk` pin differs between
the source commit's tree and the target tree, and that an app
touched by the patch (transitively) depends on. Advisory only.

source.description: Pin at the source commit, e.g. `hex 2.16.0`.

target.description: Pin at the target tree, e.g. `hex 2.13.0`.

Diagnostics.description:
Series-wide diagnostic envelope. Strictly separate from `Verdict`
so untracked-call signals never leak into machine-readable verdicts.

already_present.description:
Advisory: the patch's content appears to already exist on the
target (tier-1 identical patch, tier-2 content tally, or both).

already_present_skipped.description: Why already-present detection was skipped, when it was.

context_refs_missing.description:
In-scope references on *context* lines that do not resolve at
some pin, per module. Pre-existing target facts: never reasons.

dep_pin_divergence.description:
Dep pins that diverge between source and target trees and are
reachable from the apps this patch touches.

indirect_call_checks.description:
What the indirect-reference check (meck expectations and rpc
forms) did with each recognized occurrence: resolved against the
target module, or seen with an unreadable arity and withheld.

local_call_shape_checks.description:
The local-call twin: resolved unqualified calls, compared or
withheld. Kept apart from the qualified tally so one axis's
coverage never reads as the other's.

macro_value_checks.description:
Same-file `-define` value comparisons over macros the patch
uses: compared, or withheld and why.

missing_test_modules.description:
Per-`_SUITE.erl` map of `helper_module -> call_site_count`. The
always-on diagnostic counterpart of
`Reason::TestModuleSymbolMissing`: emitted by the parse pass
even without a target tree (which is why the inner key is the
`ModuleName` rather than a resolved-or-not bit). When
`--target-repo-dir-path` is supplied the resolver re-walks this
map and promotes the absent ones to typed reasons. The nested
`BTreeMap` shape keeps the JSON envelope serialisable without
a custom composite-key encoder.

pin_bumps.description:
Dep pins this patch itself changes or introduces in the root
`rabbitmq-components.mk`.

qualified_call_shape_checks.description:
What the live qualified-call gate's return-shape check did with
each first-party resolved call: compared, or withheld and why.

suggested_suites.description:
SUITE names worth running for the patch, derived from touched paths.
Populated even when the verdict promotes to `Inapplicable` so that
schema-only and config-only diffs still surface relevant suites.

unattributed_paths.description:
Touched paths no configured project owns, tallied by their
first two path components. The breadcrumb behind an
`Inapplicable { Untracked }` verdict.

HunkTally.description: Per-file hunk counters for the content-presence check.

oneOf.description:
Every changed `.erl` hunk is a Variant A unwrap: dropping
`-ifdef(TEST).` or `-endif.` around an `-export(...)` directive,
or rewriting `-compile(export_all).` to an explicit
`-export([...])`. No call sites, no specs, no bodies touched —
only test-visibility metadata.

The patch touches Erlang surface but every referenced symbol
resolves to the self-pin or to a local definition: every
tracked-dep pin sees zero in-scope references. Without this
reason the operator would see a wall of vacuous `Compatible`
rows for a patch that backhopper genuinely has no signal on.

Every touched path lives in a sibling project's scope, not this
pin's. The pin has nothing to say about the patch. `project`
names the first sibling project (alphabetical) that owns the
out-of-scope paths.

Every touched path is unclaimed by any configured project's
scan_paths or app_roots. Vendored files, docs, build scripts.

`--target-repo-dir-path` was supplied and every touched path
is missing from the target tree, with no configured
translation mapping any of them. The patch as written does
not apply to the target.

IncludeDirective.description:
`-include` and `-include_lib` are syntactically distinct: the
former takes a relative-to-source path, the latter an
`application/include/file.hrl` shape resolved through OTP's lib
path. The variant preserves which form the source used so the
remediation text can match.

IndirectCallForm.description:
Which recognized call form carried an indirect MFA reference. Names
the innermost form: a meck expectation reached through an rpc helper
is `MeckExpect`, not the helper.

IndirectCallTally.description:
What the indirect-reference check did with each recognized form
occurrence. `checked` counts deduplicated resolved sites, the same
dedup the reasons use; flagged sites are visible in the reasons,
not double-counted here.

checked.description:
Module first-party, export and definition sets readable: the
membership check ran.

withheld_dynamic.description:
Module and function were literal atoms but the arity source was
not statically readable: a variable argument list, a list with a
cons tail, or a non-literal arity argument.

MacroValueTally.description:
What the macro-value check did with each `?MACRO` the patch uses:
compared, or withheld and why. Same-file `-define`s only; anything
reached another way is withheld, never guessed.

compared.description:
Defined exactly once same-file on both sides; values compared.
Drift is visible in the reasons, not double-counted here.

withheld_definition_elsewhere.description:
Not defined same-file on both sides: the definition lives in an
include, or moved between files across the trees.

withheld_multiple_defines.description:
Defined more than once in the file on either side (`-ifdef`
branches): either value could be live.

withheld_no_source.description: The touched file was not readable on the source side.

NeedsPin.description:
The minimum pin that satisfies a missing-symbol reason: the typed
ordering payload q-port turns into a "bump must land first" edge.

PatchFacts.description: Source classifiers on the patch. Strictly separate from `Verdict` reasons.

PathApplyOutcome.description:
How one touched path is predicted to apply to the target tree.
Ranked by [`PathApplyOutcome::severity`]; payload-carrying variants
keep the enum out of `Ord`.

oneOf.description: Every hunk's preimage matches at its expected line.

Applies, but at least one hunk's preimage was found at a shifted
line. `line_delta` is the largest-magnitude shift.
The path could not be assessed; stated, never silent.

At least one hunk predicts a conflict. `kind` is the worst
conflict kind across the path's hunks.

PinBump.description:
A dep pin the candidate commit itself changes or introduces in the
root `rabbitmq-components.mk`. Advisory only: the verdict on a
bump-only diff stays `Inapplicable`, this is the evidence behind it.

from.description:
Pin before the commit, e.g. `hex 2.16.0`; `None` when the
commit introduces the pin.

status.description:
Snapshot-store assessment of the bumped-to version. Detection
is a pure function of the patch and may be cached; the store's
contents are not a cache-key input, so this field is filled
post-cache and cached values carry `None`.

PinPayload.description:
On-wire pin shape used inside `BatchQuery`. Distinct from
`crate::model::pin::Pin` because the wire form is a `(project, tag)`
projection without the resolution machinery.

PrCommit.description: One commit on the PR-branch side of a 2-parent merge.

PrCommitKind.description:
Classification of a PR-branch commit's role.

`#[non_exhaustive]` so future, richer taxonomies (test-only,
docs-only, dependency-bump, etc.) can add variants without a
breaking change.

oneOf.description: Default: substantive change worth reviewing.

Subject matched the conflict-resolution catalog AND the file
set was a strict subset of prior PR-branch commits.
Subject indicated the commit applied code-review feedback.
`git --fixup` auto-generated or the manual `fixup:` convention.
Subject was `WIP` or bare `Cleanup`.

first_seen_at_tag.description:
Earliest snapshot tag strictly later than the pin where the
symbol appears. `Some` reclassifies the reason as
adaptable: land the dep pin bump first.

expected_available_at.description:
Earliest snapshot tag strictly later than the pin exporting
the expected arity. Same bump-first semantics as
`MissingSymbol::first_seen_at_tag`.

oneOf.description:
The contiguous preimage block (Context and Removed lines from
the hunk) was found verbatim at a different starting line.
Cherry-pick adapters handle this with the `-x` trailer; the
operator just needs the delta to confirm the patch's intent
still applies.

The hunk's preimage matches, but its added lines land at a file
edge where the target already has divergent content the base
lacked: an add/add a contiguous preimage match cannot see. The
3-way cherry-pick conflicts where the preimage-only check reads
clean. Non-blocking: the operator resolves the overlap.

The preimage block does not appear anywhere in the file. The
patch was authored against a tree where the lines existed; on
this pin they don't. Structurally inapplicable: the operator
needs an excerpt to reason about why.

Call-site argument shapes don't satisfy any clause head at the
pin. Emitted when both the call and the pin's clause patterns
are concrete enough to compare; `Unknown` on either side is the
escape hatch that suppresses the reason.

Patch references an MFA owned by the self-project but absent from the
resolved self-snapshot. `suggested_source_for_prereq` is filled only
with `--suggest-prereqs`.

Pre-flight syntactic damage in a touched file: an unresolved
merge-conflict marker, an exported function with no definition, etc.
Patch changes a `-callback` signature; an implementer still has the old one.
Patch removes a required callback; implementer still exports it.
Patch adds a required callback; implementer is missing the export.
Patch touches a path absent on pin, but a module of the same basename exists elsewhere.
Wire-bearing macro value differs between source and pin.
`version/0` advanced without the matching historical-implementation module.
Function bodies drifted at the same advertised `version/0`. Mixed-version cluster risk.
`version/0` decreased pin → patch.
Spec return shape differs between source and pin for a referenced MFA.

A type-reference inside a `-spec`, `-callback`, `-type`, or
`-opaque` attribute resolves to a name and arity that the pin
does not expose via `-export_type`. Non-blocking: a missing
type alias is a dialyzer-level concern, not a load-time crash.

A touched path is absent from the target tree, but a
configured `[[path_translation]]` rewrites it to a path that
does exist on the target. Non-blocking: the operator (or the
cherry-pick driver) rewrites the path before applying.

A touched path is absent on the target while others are present
and no `[[path_translation]]` rewrites it. Non-blocking: dropping
the hunks for this path lets the rest apply. The all-absent case
is `InapplicableReason::PathsMissingOnTarget`.

A `_SUITE.erl` file in the patch references `missing_module:f/n`
where `missing_module` resolves to no source file under any
configured `FamilyDefaults.test_helper_search_paths` on the
target tree. The cherry-pick compiles and the SUITE may even
load, but every call to the missing helper crashes at runtime:
the failure pattern that bit the Jun 2026 v4.1.x → v4.0.x round
(the `amqp_utils:connection_config/1` undef in
`amqp10_connection_max_SUITE`). Non-blocking by default: the
diagnostic equivalent (`Diagnostics.missing_test_modules`)
always fires; the `Reason` variant fires only when
`--target-repo-dir-path` is supplied and the resolution is
authoritative.

A touched `.erl` declares `-behaviour(behaviour)` (or
`-behavior(...)`) where `behaviour` resolves to no source
module on the target tree. `erlc` compiles with a warning,
then hook dispatch crashes at runtime. Sister verdict to the
existing `BehaviourCallback*` variants which model implementer
drift; this one catches the missing-behaviour-module case the
existing variants do not.

A touched `.erl` or `.hrl` declares `-include(path)` or
`-include_lib(app/include/file.hrl)` against a target tree that
does not ship the resolved header. Compile-time failure rather
than runtime, but same user-facing shape as
`TestModuleSymbolMissing`: looked fine on source, broken on
target.

A touched `.erl` or `.hrl` file references `?MACRO` on an added
line, but `MACRO` is defined nowhere the target tree reaches (not
in the file, its includes, or the patch itself) and is not
predefined. Compiles on source, dangles on target. Non-blocking:
the operator drops or adapts the reference.

A touched `.erl` or `.hrl` file uses `#record{}` on an added
line, but `record` is defined nowhere the target tree reaches and
is not added by the patch. Sister of `MacroUndefinedOnTarget` for
the record namespace; non-blocking.

A touched `.erl` file calls an unqualified `f/a` on an added line
that the target version of the same module neither defines,
exports, imports, nor inherits as an auto-imported BIF. The
function-namespace counterpart; non-blocking.

A touched `.erl` file calls a qualified `m:f/a` on an added line
whose module is a first-party module present on the target tree,
but the target version of that module does not export `f/a` (and
the patch does not add it). The qualified counterpart of
`LocalCallUndefinedOnTarget`, resolved against the called
module's exports. Withheld when any pin snapshot already covers
the module, when it is absent from the tree, or when its export
surface is not fully readable. Non-blocking.

A qualified `m:f/a` call that resolves against the target tree
has a target-tree `-spec` return shape that disagrees with its
source-tree `-spec`. Sister of `ReturnShapeMismatch` for the
live, snapshot-free first-party axis: same comparator,
non-blocking like the rest of that axis. Only evaluated once the
call is confirmed to resolve; withheld when either side lacks a
`-spec`.

An unqualified call that resolves against the target module's
own definitions has a target-tree `-spec` return shape that
disagrees with its source-tree `-spec`. The local twin of
`QualifiedCallReturnShapeDrift`; imported resolutions are
withheld, since the callee's spec lives in another module.

A `?MACRO` the patch uses is defined in the touched file itself
on both trees, exactly once each, and the normalized `-define`
bodies disagree: the compile-clean, behavior-divergent class.
Withheld for definitions reached any other way. Non-blocking.

The target's version of a behaviour the patch declares requires
a callback the source's version does not, and the target does
not list it as optional: an implementation written against the
source is missing it. `line` is the `-behaviour` attribute's
line in the touched file. Non-blocking.

A callback both trees' versions of a declared behaviour declare
has a different normalized signature on the target. The whole
signature is compared, not just the return half: a callback
contract's argument types are the implementer's obligation.
Non-blocking.

Declared versioned-machine module is touched but the snapshot
has no recorded `versioned_machine_version` on `side`.
Non-blocking.

Declared wire constants are touched but the snapshot's
`wire_constants` vector lacks the listed macros on `side`.
`macros` is sorted alphabetically. Non-blocking.

A first-party `m:f/a` referenced as arguments to a mocking or
rpc form (a meck expectation, `rpc:call`, `erpc:call`, or a CT
broker rpc helper) is neither exported nor defined by the target
tree's module. Non-blocking: a meck expectation can install a
function the module never had, so absence proves drift, not
failure.

RefOrigin.description:
Which side of the hunk a reference was extracted from. `Added`
lines are requirements the patch introduces; `Context` lines are
pre-existing facts about the target and never drive verdicts.
`Added` orders first so a kind-level dedup keeps the stronger
origin.

ResolverClass.description: A class of symbol whose presence a backport can dangle on.

ResolverCoverage.description:
The set of classes a producer checks, stamped on a verdict envelope
so a corpus row self-describes its producer's coverage. Stores only
the checked set: `unchecked` is derived, so a class can never be in
both or neither.

ShapeCheckTally.description:
What the live qualified-call gate's return-shape check did with
each first-party resolved call. Never reasons: a withhold is not a
finding, but a round where most calls are shape-blind must read
differently from a round where all of them were compared.

compared.description:
Both sides had a `-spec` that parsed to a known type; the shapes
were compared. Drift is visible in the reasons, not double-counted
here.

withheld_imported.description:
The call resolved through an `-import`: the callee's `-spec`
lives in another module, so the calling module's tables cannot
compare it. Local-call axis only.

withheld_no_source.description:
The callee module was not readable on the source side: no
checkout was supplied, or the checkout has no file at the
module's path (a defaulted `--repo-dir-path` that is not the
source tree lands here, not in `withheld_no_spec`).

withheld_no_spec.description: One or both sides declare no `-spec` for the called function.

withheld_unknown_type.description:
Both sides have a spec but at least one parses to
`SpecType::Unknown`.

SnapshotSide.description: Which side of a snapshot comparison the data is missing from.

oneOf.description:
A function reference whose arity could not be determined from
the source line (the call's closing paren sits on a later
line). Resolves against a snapshot when *any* export carries
the name; never produces an arity mismatch.

TargetMatch.description:
A target commit found to carry the candidate's patch. The subject
rides along so consumers can auto-fill exclusion reasons without
a second git query.

TargetMatchKind.description:
How a tier-1 already-present match against the target branch was
established.

oneOf.description:
A walked target commit's `-x` trailer names the candidate (or
one of its trailer origins or inner PR commits).

One of the candidate's own trailer origins is already an
ancestor of the target tip.

A walked target commit's normalized patch hash equals the
candidate's.

TestCallSite.description:
One `Module:Function/Arity` reference inside a `_SUITE.erl` that
resolves to a module absent on the target tree. Carries the line
number so the operator can jump straight to the call site.

TouchedKinds.description:
Per-pin tally of file kinds the patch touched. Lets `promote_inapplicable`
tell a real green check from a diff with nothing analyzable to check.

only_self_surface.description:
The patch touches Erlang surface but references no tracked-dep
API (every non-self pin sees zero in-scope references). The CLI
sets this after `evaluate_series` when a self-pin is present
and every non-self pin's `tracked_refs` is empty; see
`InapplicableReason::OnlySelfSurfaceTouched`.

only_test_visibility.description:
Every changed `.erl` hunk is a Variant A unwrap of test-only
`-ifdef(TEST)` machinery around an `-export` directive (see
`InapplicableReason::OnlyTestVisibilityChanged`). When true,
the patch touches Erlang surface but adds no semantic
content, so an empty reason set should promote to
`Inapplicable` instead of `Compatible`.

Unanalyzed.description:
Counts of call sites the analyzer could not resolve: `apply/3`-style
BIFs, and dispatch through a variable module or function. Informational only.

UnassessedReason.description:
Why a path's apply outcome could not be assessed. The `Ord` only
breaks merge ties deterministically; it is not a severity.

oneOf.description: The diff marks the file binary; there is no hunk text to match.
The target blob exists but is not valid UTF-8.

VerdictFingerprint.description:
A verdict's stable identity for measurement: equal fingerprints
mean the same patch against the same target and pins, whatever
backhopper version produced either side.

batch_payload.description: Top-level payload of a `check batch` envelope.

fingerprint_version.description:
The fingerprint generation this producer stamped. Lets a corpus
spanning a bump segregate generations instead of reading an
unexplained zero-match. `None` for a producer that predates it.

resolver_coverage.description:
Symbol classes this producer checks. A corpus row keeps it so the
fold routes bug-vs-gap against the producing binary, not the one
running the fold. `None` for a producer that predates the field.

self_projects.description:
Projects evaluated as the backport subject itself, excluded from
the tracked-dependency tally. `None` means the producing binary
predates the field, not "no self project": a current producer
always emits `Some`, even when empty, so it is never skipped.

batch_payload.title: BatchPayload

CacheLevel.description: Which workspace cache an entry belongs to.

oneOf.description: `.verdict_cache/by-input/`: SHA-keyed verdict entries.
`.verdict_cache/by-content/`: content-keyed verdict entries.
`.siblings_doctor_cache/`: `siblings doctor` run entries.

alias.description: True for `by-input` entries minted from a content-level hit.

commit.description: The evaluated commit, for verdict entries that carry one.

key.description:
The entry's key hash (the file-name stem after the format
prefix); unique prefixes of it address entries in `show` and
`evict`.

series.description: The series or pin target, when the pre-image names one.

cache_mutation_payload.description: Payload for `cache evict`, `cache prune`, and `cache clear`.
cache_mutation_payload.title: CacheMutationPayload

CacheLevel.description: Which workspace cache an entry belongs to.

oneOf.description: `.verdict_cache/by-input/`: SHA-keyed verdict entries.
`.verdict_cache/by-content/`: content-keyed verdict entries.
`.siblings_doctor_cache/`: `siblings doctor` run entries.

cache_show_payload.description: The `cache show` payload: one entry, pre-image included.

alias.description:
True for `by-input` entries minted as aliases of a
content-level hit.

key_inputs.description: The canonical-JSON key pre-image stored inside the entry.

value.description: The full stored value, under `--full` only.

verdict_summary.description:
Verdict counts for verdict entries; absent for siblings
entries.

cache_show_payload.title: CacheShowPayload

cache_stats_payload.description: The `cache stats` payload, covering both workspace caches.

aliases.description: `by-input` entries minted as aliases of a content-level hit.

oldest_entry_at.description:
RFC3339 write times of the oldest and newest entries across
every level; absent when all caches are empty.

cache_stats_payload.title: CacheStatsPayload

description: v13 adds the apply axis: `SeriesEvaluation` and `BatchResult` gain `apply`, a per-path forecast of whether the patch applies to the target tree as written (clean, drifted, unassessed, or a predicted conflict). The field is absent when no target context was supplied, so absence means the axis was not evaluated, never that it was clean. The forecast is independent of every pin verdict: an all-inapplicable row still carries its predicted conflicts, and the round clearance and exit code fold over both axes.

command.description: Verb identifier in kebab-case, e.g. "check merge".

AlreadyPresent.description:
Advisory: the patch's content appears to already exist on the
target. Never affects the verdict; q-port and the operator own
the exclusion decision.

content.description: Tier-2 tally: the post-image is (partly) present in the tree.

identical.description: Tier-1 hit: an identical patch landed on the target.

AlreadyPresentSkipped.description:
Why already-present detection could not run. Emitted instead of
silence: an invisible skip would read as "not present".

oneOf.description:
The candidate commit object is absent from the target object
store (an unfetched branch, usually).
The candidate and the target tip share no history.
The target-side walk failed (shallow clone, corrupt object).

ApplyConflictKind.description:
The apply outcomes a divergence predictor consumes, ordered by
severity: a higher variant outranks a lower one on the same path, so
dedup to one conflict per path is a `max`.

ApplyForecast.description:
Per-path apply prediction for one `(commit, series)` row, computed
from the target tree. Present exactly when a target context was
supplied.

paths.description:
Every assessed touched path, including ones absent on the
target (`Conflict { FileAbsent }`).

oneOf.description: Variable identifier (starts with `_` or capital letter).
Atom literal: `foo`, `'quoted atom'`.
Integer literal.
Float literal.
Binary literal: `<<...>>`.
List literal: `[...]`.
Tuple literal: `{...}` (size is the number of elements).
Record reference: `#name{...}`.
String literal: `"..."`.
Anonymous fun: `fun ... end` or `fun mod:f/A`.
Anything the extractor cannot classify. Always matches.

`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`, or `||||||| ` marker present in a
touched file. The cherry-pick driver left a conflict unresolved.

`-export([f/N])` line without a matching clause defining `f/N`.
Compiles, then crashes at runtime on the first call.

BumpStatus.description: What the snapshot store knows about a bumped-to pin version.

oneOf.description: The bumped dep is not a tracked project; nothing to vet.
No snapshot for the bumped-to version; `note` carries the remedy.
`<<<<<<<` line: start of the local side.
`=======` line: divider between sides.
`>>>>>>>` line: end of the incoming side.
`||||||| ` line: base ancestor marker from a 3-way diff.

ContentPresence.description:
Tier-2 advisory: how much of the patch's post-image already exists
in the named pin's tree. A tally, never a boolean: partial presence
is common and the fraction is the signal.

pin.description:
The pin whose evaluation produced the tally. In cross-branch
mode the self pin resolves to the target branch, so its tally
is the target-tree answer.

DepPinDivergence.description:
A dependency whose `rabbitmq-components.mk` pin differs between
the source commit's tree and the target tree, and that an app
touched by the patch (transitively) depends on. Advisory only.

source.description: Pin at the source commit, e.g. `hex 2.16.0`.

target.description: Pin at the target tree, e.g. `hex 2.13.0`.

Diagnostics.description:
Series-wide diagnostic envelope. Strictly separate from `Verdict`
so untracked-call signals never leak into machine-readable verdicts.

already_present.description:
Advisory: the patch's content appears to already exist on the
target (tier-1 identical patch, tier-2 content tally, or both).

already_present_skipped.description: Why already-present detection was skipped, when it was.

context_refs_missing.description:
In-scope references on *context* lines that do not resolve at
some pin, per module. Pre-existing target facts: never reasons.

dep_pin_divergence.description:
Dep pins that diverge between source and target trees and are
reachable from the apps this patch touches.

indirect_call_checks.description:
What the indirect-reference check (meck expectations and rpc
forms) did with each recognized occurrence: resolved against the
target module, or seen with an unreadable arity and withheld.

local_call_shape_checks.description:
The local-call twin: resolved unqualified calls, compared or
withheld. Kept apart from the qualified tally so one axis's
coverage never reads as the other's.

macro_value_checks.description:
Same-file `-define` value comparisons over macros the patch
uses: compared, or withheld and why.

missing_test_modules.description:
Per-`_SUITE.erl` map of `helper_module -> call_site_count`. The
always-on diagnostic counterpart of
`Reason::TestModuleSymbolMissing`: emitted by the parse pass
even without a target tree (which is why the inner key is the
`ModuleName` rather than a resolved-or-not bit). When
`--target-repo-dir-path` is supplied the resolver re-walks this
map and promotes the absent ones to typed reasons. The nested
`BTreeMap` shape keeps the JSON envelope serialisable without
a custom composite-key encoder.

pin_bumps.description:
Dep pins this patch itself changes or introduces in the root
`rabbitmq-components.mk`.

qualified_call_shape_checks.description:
What the live qualified-call gate's return-shape check did with
each first-party resolved call: compared, or withheld and why.

suggested_suites.description:
SUITE names worth running for the patch, derived from touched paths.
Populated even when the verdict promotes to `Inapplicable` so that
schema-only and config-only diffs still surface relevant suites.

unattributed_paths.description:
Touched paths no configured project owns, tallied by their
first two path components. The breadcrumb behind an
`Inapplicable { Untracked }` verdict.

HunkTally.description: Per-file hunk counters for the content-presence check.

oneOf.description:
Every changed `.erl` hunk is a Variant A unwrap: dropping
`-ifdef(TEST).` or `-endif.` around an `-export(...)` directive,
or rewriting `-compile(export_all).` to an explicit
`-export([...])`. No call sites, no specs, no bodies touched —
only test-visibility metadata.

The patch touches Erlang surface but every referenced symbol
resolves to the self-pin or to a local definition: every
tracked-dep pin sees zero in-scope references. Without this
reason the operator would see a wall of vacuous `Compatible`
rows for a patch that backhopper genuinely has no signal on.

Every touched path lives in a sibling project's scope, not this
pin's. The pin has nothing to say about the patch. `project`
names the first sibling project (alphabetical) that owns the
out-of-scope paths.

Every touched path is unclaimed by any configured project's
scan_paths or app_roots. Vendored files, docs, build scripts.

`--target-repo-dir-path` was supplied and every touched path
is missing from the target tree, with no configured
translation mapping any of them. The patch as written does
not apply to the target.

IncludeDirective.description:
`-include` and `-include_lib` are syntactically distinct: the
former takes a relative-to-source path, the latter an
`application/include/file.hrl` shape resolved through OTP's lib
path. The variant preserves which form the source used so the
remediation text can match.

IndirectCallForm.description:
Which recognized call form carried an indirect MFA reference. Names
the innermost form: a meck expectation reached through an rpc helper
is `MeckExpect`, not the helper.

IndirectCallTally.description:
What the indirect-reference check did with each recognized form
occurrence. `checked` counts deduplicated resolved sites, the same
dedup the reasons use; flagged sites are visible in the reasons,
not double-counted here.

checked.description:
Module first-party, export and definition sets readable: the
membership check ran.

withheld_dynamic.description:
Module and function were literal atoms but the arity source was
not statically readable: a variable argument list, a list with a
cons tail, or a non-literal arity argument.

MacroValueTally.description:
What the macro-value check did with each `?MACRO` the patch uses:
compared, or withheld and why. Same-file `-define`s only; anything
reached another way is withheld, never guessed.

compared.description:
Defined exactly once same-file on both sides; values compared.
Drift is visible in the reasons, not double-counted here.

withheld_definition_elsewhere.description:
Not defined same-file on both sides: the definition lives in an
include, or moved between files across the trees.

withheld_multiple_defines.description:
Defined more than once in the file on either side (`-ifdef`
branches): either value could be live.

withheld_no_source.description: The touched file was not readable on the source side.

NeedsPin.description:
The minimum pin that satisfies a missing-symbol reason: the typed
ordering payload q-port turns into a "bump must land first" edge.

PatchFacts.description: Source classifiers on the patch. Strictly separate from `Verdict` reasons.

PathApplyOutcome.description:
How one touched path is predicted to apply to the target tree.
Ranked by [`PathApplyOutcome::severity`]; payload-carrying variants
keep the enum out of `Ord`.

oneOf.description: Every hunk's preimage matches at its expected line.

Applies, but at least one hunk's preimage was found at a shifted
line. `line_delta` is the largest-magnitude shift.
The path could not be assessed; stated, never silent.

At least one hunk predicts a conflict. `kind` is the worst
conflict kind across the path's hunks.

PinBump.description:
A dep pin the candidate commit itself changes or introduces in the
root `rabbitmq-components.mk`. Advisory only: the verdict on a
bump-only diff stays `Inapplicable`, this is the evidence behind it.

from.description:
Pin before the commit, e.g. `hex 2.16.0`; `None` when the
commit introduces the pin.

status.description:
Snapshot-store assessment of the bumped-to version. Detection
is a pure function of the patch and may be cached; the store's
contents are not a cache-key input, so this field is filled
post-cache and cached values carry `None`.

PrCommit.description: One commit on the PR-branch side of a 2-parent merge.

PrCommitKind.description:
Classification of a PR-branch commit's role.

`#[non_exhaustive]` so future, richer taxonomies (test-only,
docs-only, dependency-bump, etc.) can add variants without a
breaking change.

oneOf.description: Default: substantive change worth reviewing.

Subject matched the conflict-resolution catalog AND the file
set was a strict subset of prior PR-branch commits.
Subject indicated the commit applied code-review feedback.
`git --fixup` auto-generated or the manual `fixup:` convention.
Subject was `WIP` or bare `Cleanup`.

first_seen_at_tag.description:
Earliest snapshot tag strictly later than the pin where the
symbol appears. `Some` reclassifies the reason as
adaptable: land the dep pin bump first.

expected_available_at.description:
Earliest snapshot tag strictly later than the pin exporting
the expected arity. Same bump-first semantics as
`MissingSymbol::first_seen_at_tag`.

oneOf.description:
The contiguous preimage block (Context and Removed lines from
the hunk) was found verbatim at a different starting line.
Cherry-pick adapters handle this with the `-x` trailer; the
operator just needs the delta to confirm the patch's intent
still applies.

The hunk's preimage matches, but its added lines land at a file
edge where the target already has divergent content the base
lacked: an add/add a contiguous preimage match cannot see. The
3-way cherry-pick conflicts where the preimage-only check reads
clean. Non-blocking: the operator resolves the overlap.

The preimage block does not appear anywhere in the file. The
patch was authored against a tree where the lines existed; on
this pin they don't. Structurally inapplicable: the operator
needs an excerpt to reason about why.

Call-site argument shapes don't satisfy any clause head at the
pin. Emitted when both the call and the pin's clause patterns
are concrete enough to compare; `Unknown` on either side is the
escape hatch that suppresses the reason.

Patch references an MFA owned by the self-project but absent from the
resolved self-snapshot. `suggested_source_for_prereq` is filled only
with `--suggest-prereqs`.

Pre-flight syntactic damage in a touched file: an unresolved
merge-conflict marker, an exported function with no definition, etc.
Patch changes a `-callback` signature; an implementer still has the old one.
Patch removes a required callback; implementer still exports it.
Patch adds a required callback; implementer is missing the export.
Patch touches a path absent on pin, but a module of the same basename exists elsewhere.
Wire-bearing macro value differs between source and pin.
`version/0` advanced without the matching historical-implementation module.
Function bodies drifted at the same advertised `version/0`. Mixed-version cluster risk.
`version/0` decreased pin → patch.
Spec return shape differs between source and pin for a referenced MFA.

A type-reference inside a `-spec`, `-callback`, `-type`, or
`-opaque` attribute resolves to a name and arity that the pin
does not expose via `-export_type`. Non-blocking: a missing
type alias is a dialyzer-level concern, not a load-time crash.

A touched path is absent from the target tree, but a
configured `[[path_translation]]` rewrites it to a path that
does exist on the target. Non-blocking: the operator (or the
cherry-pick driver) rewrites the path before applying.

A touched path is absent on the target while others are present
and no `[[path_translation]]` rewrites it. Non-blocking: dropping
the hunks for this path lets the rest apply. The all-absent case
is `InapplicableReason::PathsMissingOnTarget`.

A `_SUITE.erl` file in the patch references `missing_module:f/n`
where `missing_module` resolves to no source file under any
configured `FamilyDefaults.test_helper_search_paths` on the
target tree. The cherry-pick compiles and the SUITE may even
load, but every call to the missing helper crashes at runtime:
the failure pattern that bit the Jun 2026 v4.1.x → v4.0.x round
(the `amqp_utils:connection_config/1` undef in
`amqp10_connection_max_SUITE`). Non-blocking by default: the
diagnostic equivalent (`Diagnostics.missing_test_modules`)
always fires; the `Reason` variant fires only when
`--target-repo-dir-path` is supplied and the resolution is
authoritative.

A touched `.erl` declares `-behaviour(behaviour)` (or
`-behavior(...)`) where `behaviour` resolves to no source
module on the target tree. `erlc` compiles with a warning,
then hook dispatch crashes at runtime. Sister verdict to the
existing `BehaviourCallback*` variants which model implementer
drift; this one catches the missing-behaviour-module case the
existing variants do not.

A touched `.erl` or `.hrl` declares `-include(path)` or
`-include_lib(app/include/file.hrl)` against a target tree that
does not ship the resolved header. Compile-time failure rather
than runtime, but same user-facing shape as
`TestModuleSymbolMissing`: looked fine on source, broken on
target.

A touched `.erl` or `.hrl` file references `?MACRO` on an added
line, but `MACRO` is defined nowhere the target tree reaches (not
in the file, its includes, or the patch itself) and is not
predefined. Compiles on source, dangles on target. Non-blocking:
the operator drops or adapts the reference.

A touched `.erl` or `.hrl` file uses `#record{}` on an added
line, but `record` is defined nowhere the target tree reaches and
is not added by the patch. Sister of `MacroUndefinedOnTarget` for
the record namespace; non-blocking.

A touched `.erl` file calls an unqualified `f/a` on an added line
that the target version of the same module neither defines,
exports, imports, nor inherits as an auto-imported BIF. The
function-namespace counterpart; non-blocking.

A touched `.erl` file calls a qualified `m:f/a` on an added line
whose module is a first-party module present on the target tree,
but the target version of that module does not export `f/a` (and
the patch does not add it). The qualified counterpart of
`LocalCallUndefinedOnTarget`, resolved against the called
module's exports. Withheld when any pin snapshot already covers
the module, when it is absent from the tree, or when its export
surface is not fully readable. Non-blocking.

A qualified `m:f/a` call that resolves against the target tree
has a target-tree `-spec` return shape that disagrees with its
source-tree `-spec`. Sister of `ReturnShapeMismatch` for the
live, snapshot-free first-party axis: same comparator,
non-blocking like the rest of that axis. Only evaluated once the
call is confirmed to resolve; withheld when either side lacks a
`-spec`.

An unqualified call that resolves against the target module's
own definitions has a target-tree `-spec` return shape that
disagrees with its source-tree `-spec`. The local twin of
`QualifiedCallReturnShapeDrift`; imported resolutions are
withheld, since the callee's spec lives in another module.

A `?MACRO` the patch uses is defined in the touched file itself
on both trees, exactly once each, and the normalized `-define`
bodies disagree: the compile-clean, behavior-divergent class.
Withheld for definitions reached any other way. Non-blocking.

The target's version of a behaviour the patch declares requires
a callback the source's version does not, and the target does
not list it as optional: an implementation written against the
source is missing it. `line` is the `-behaviour` attribute's
line in the touched file. Non-blocking.

A callback both trees' versions of a declared behaviour declare
has a different normalized signature on the target. The whole
signature is compared, not just the return half: a callback
contract's argument types are the implementer's obligation.
Non-blocking.

Declared versioned-machine module is touched but the snapshot
has no recorded `versioned_machine_version` on `side`.
Non-blocking.

Declared wire constants are touched but the snapshot's
`wire_constants` vector lacks the listed macros on `side`.
`macros` is sorted alphabetically. Non-blocking.

A first-party `m:f/a` referenced as arguments to a mocking or
rpc form (a meck expectation, `rpc:call`, `erpc:call`, or a CT
broker rpc helper) is neither exported nor defined by the target
tree's module. Non-blocking: a meck expectation can install a
function the module never had, so absence proves drift, not
failure.

RefOrigin.description:
Which side of the hunk a reference was extracted from. `Added`
lines are requirements the patch introduces; `Context` lines are
pre-existing facts about the target and never drive verdicts.
`Added` orders first so a kind-level dedup keeps the stronger
origin.

ShapeCheckTally.description:
What the live qualified-call gate's return-shape check did with
each first-party resolved call. Never reasons: a withhold is not a
finding, but a round where most calls are shape-blind must read
differently from a round where all of them were compared.

compared.description:
Both sides had a `-spec` that parsed to a known type; the shapes
were compared. Drift is visible in the reasons, not double-counted
here.

withheld_imported.description:
The call resolved through an `-import`: the callee's `-spec`
lives in another module, so the calling module's tables cannot
compare it. Local-call axis only.

withheld_no_source.description:
The callee module was not readable on the source side: no
checkout was supplied, or the checkout has no file at the
module's path (a defaulted `--repo-dir-path` that is not the
source tree lands here, not in `withheld_no_spec`).

withheld_no_spec.description: One or both sides declare no `-spec` for the called function.

withheld_unknown_type.description:
Both sides have a spec but at least one parses to
`SpecType::Unknown`.

SnapshotSide.description: Which side of a snapshot comparison the data is missing from.

oneOf.description:
A function reference whose arity could not be determined from
the source line (the call's closing paren sits on a later
line). Resolves against a snapshot when *any* export carries
the name; never produces an arity mismatch.

TargetMatch.description:
A target commit found to carry the candidate's patch. The subject
rides along so consumers can auto-fill exclusion reasons without
a second git query.

TargetMatchKind.description:
How a tier-1 already-present match against the target branch was
established.

oneOf.description:
A walked target commit's `-x` trailer names the candidate (or
one of its trailer origins or inner PR commits).

One of the candidate's own trailer origins is already an
ancestor of the target tip.

A walked target commit's normalized patch hash equals the
candidate's.

TestCallSite.description:
One `Module:Function/Arity` reference inside a `_SUITE.erl` that
resolves to a module absent on the target tree. Carries the line
number so the operator can jump straight to the call site.

TouchedKinds.description:
Per-pin tally of file kinds the patch touched. Lets `promote_inapplicable`
tell a real green check from a diff with nothing analyzable to check.

only_self_surface.description:
The patch touches Erlang surface but references no tracked-dep
API (every non-self pin sees zero in-scope references). The CLI
sets this after `evaluate_series` when a self-pin is present
and every non-self pin's `tracked_refs` is empty; see
`InapplicableReason::OnlySelfSurfaceTouched`.

only_test_visibility.description:
Every changed `.erl` hunk is a Variant A unwrap of test-only
`-ifdef(TEST)` machinery around an `-export` directive (see
`InapplicableReason::OnlyTestVisibilityChanged`). When true,
the patch touches Erlang surface but adds no semantic
content, so an empty reason set should promote to
`Inapplicable` instead of `Compatible`.

Unanalyzed.description:
Counts of call sites the analyzer could not resolve: `apply/3`-style
BIFs, and dispatch through a variable module or function. Informational only.

UnassessedReason.description:
Why a path's apply outcome could not be assessed. The `Ord` only
breaks merge ties deterministically; it is not a severity.

oneOf.description: The diff marks the file binary; there is no hunk text to match.
The target blob exists but is not valid UTF-8.

data.description:
The output of `Patch::evaluate_series`: verdicts plus diagnostics plus
`PatchFacts` (source classifiers that drive downstream policy without
being verdict reasons).

apply.description:
Apply-axis prediction for this evaluation. `None` means no
target context was supplied, so the axis was not evaluated:
never "clean". A producer with a target context always emits
`Some`, even when the patch touched zero files.

pr_commits.description:
Inner PR-branch commits for 2-parent merge SHAs. `None` for
non-2-parent merges and non-merge SHAs.

Do NOT add `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`. The
`None` vs `Some(vec![])` distinction is wire-load-bearing.

touched_paths.description:
Paths the analysed patch touched, in diff-encounter order.
Always emitted; an empty vec means the patch touched zero files.

data.title: SeriesEvaluation

exit_code.description: Process exit code carried inside the envelope; matches the process status.

schema_version.description: Wire-format schema version. Bumps when envelope shape changes.

warnings.description: Free-form CLI warnings attached to the envelope.

Confidence.description:
A clamped `[0.0, 1.0]` ranking score. Total-ordered via
`f32::total_cmp` so candidates always sort; the constructor maps
NaN to zero, so no surprising order exists to begin with.

ScoreComponents.description:
Per-factor breakdown serialised under `--explain` for operator
trust and corpus tuning.

SiblingCandidate.description:
One sibling-branch commit moving through the doctor pipeline.
`state` is flattened on the wire, so a scored candidate serialises
with `confidence` and `action` as plain row fields.

age_days.description:
Whole days between `committed_at` and the run; recomputed on
cache hits so a cached row never reports a stale age.

committed_at.description:
Committer timestamp: when the commit landed on the source
branch, which is what "how overdue is this sweep" measures.

score_components.description:
Present in memory after every scoring pass; the CLI strips it
from output unless `--explain` was given.

SiblingDriftAction.description:
Recommended operator action, computed from threshold bands here,
never re-derived by consumers.

SinceDerivation.description:
How the since-point was derived. Travels on the wire so consumers
can tell a defaulted window from an operator-chosen one.

VocabularySource.description:
Where the effective vocabulary came from. `Empty` is emitted (with
a warning) instead of silently producing a zero-candidate run.

suppressed_count.description:
Candidates dropped because they already cascaded to the
target (`-x` trailer or patch-id match): the visible proof
the suppression filter ran.

walked_count.description: First-parent commits walked across every source branch.

BroadImpactModule.description:
A modified module whose suite fanout is an outsized share of all
discovered suites. The cap drops the suites this module alone pulled
in and records this row instead, so a near-full selection driven by
one helper is never silent.

SuiteInclusionReason.description:
Why a suite was included in the plan. A suite can appear under
multiple reasons when more than one rule fires.

oneOf.description: The suite file itself appears in the diff.

Fast unit or property suite swept because its application has
modified source and the suite references at least one of the
modified modules.

Suite is in the same application as a modified module and
references that module by name.

Suite is in a different application from a modified library
module and references that module by name.
Suite was included by a user-configured rule.

A modified `.erl` is itself a behaviour module; this suite
references one of its implementers.

SuitePlanEntry.description: One entry in the plan: the suite plus every rule that included it.

SuiteRef.description:
A test-suite module reference. `module` ends in `_SUITE` by
convention but the constructor does not enforce this.

UncoveredApplication.description:
An application with modified source modules that no plan entry
covers. Advisory only: the operator picks suites from `suites`
(or learns the application has none) instead of discovering the
gap from a silent empty plan.

suites.description:
The application's discovered suites: the operator's candidate
list. Empty means the application has no tests at all.

suite_plan_payload.description:
Output of `plan()`. Entries are sorted by suite; reasons within
each entry are in rule-application order.

broad_impact.description:
Modules whose suite fanout was capped: each removed the suites it
alone pulled in, replaced by this row.

unattributed_paths.description:
Modified paths that resolve to no application, so a plan with
fewer reasons than inputs is still fully accounted for.

suite_plan_payload.title: SuitePlan

TouchedKinds.description:
Per-pin tally of file kinds the patch touched. Lets `promote_inapplicable`
tell a real green check from a diff with nothing analyzable to check.

only_self_surface.description:
The patch touches Erlang surface but references no tracked-dep
API (every non-self pin sees zero in-scope references). The CLI
sets this after `evaluate_series` when a self-pin is present
and every non-self pin's `tracked_refs` is empty; see
`InapplicableReason::OnlySelfSurfaceTouched`.

only_test_visibility.description:
Every changed `.erl` hunk is a Variant A unwrap of test-only
`-ifdef(TEST)` machinery around an `-export` directive (see
`InapplicableReason::OnlyTestVisibilityChanged`). When true,
the patch touches Erlang surface but adds no semantic
content, so an empty reason set should promote to
`Inapplicable` instead of `Compatible`.

VerdictKind.description:
Kind-only projection of `Verdict`: drops the variant payloads so a
summary row stays single-line.

summary_row.description:
One row in the summary output: a compact projection of a single
`SeriesEvaluation` result. JSON and text formatters share the type.

apply_conflicts.description:
Paths the apply forecast predicts will conflict on the target.
Zero when the forecast is clean or was not evaluated; the
verdict kind never reflects it, so the row states it itself.

parent_count.description:
Parent count of the evaluated commit; `None` for patch and PR
inputs (no commit identity) and pre-v7 envelopes.

series.description:
The series the row was evaluated against. `None` for
pin-targeted single evaluations and pre-v7 envelopes.

tracked.description:
Total tracked-dep symbol references summed over every evaluated
pin. Zero means the patch references no tracked-dep API; the
row is safe to skip at a glance.

summary_row.title: SummaryRow
